packageRules.description: One PR per dep — matches existing per-dependency Linear-ticket cadence

Pin Docker base image digests (UNK-254). Tags stay human-readable; the appended @sha256 digest gives tamper-evidence and reproducible buildkit cache behaviour. Scoped to Docker managers only — cargo/npm lockfiles already pin transitively. Digest bumps auto-merge via the auto-merge rule below: they stay libc-ABI-compatible within a Debian codename, and a sha256 bump cannot be meaningfully human-reviewed anyway (the reviewer cannot inspect layer contents from the digest). Note: minimumReleaseAge does NOT gate pin/digest update types (Renovate limitation), so digest bumps land within one schedule window with CI-green as the only check. Acceptable because all bases are Docker Official Images.

Auto-merge patch/pin/digest for Docker base images. Digest bumps cannot be meaningfully human-reviewed (the reviewer cannot inspect layer contents from a sha256) and all bases are Docker Official Images — see the pinDigests rule above for the full justification.

GitHub-owned actions (actions/*, github/*): auto-merge patch/pin/digest. Platform-trust tier — these share GitHub's own compromise boundary (if github.com itself is subverted, SHA-pinning does not save us), so a digest bump tracking first-party tag movement is auto-merged on CI-green, mirroring the Docker Official Images carve-out. Major/minor version bumps are absent here, so v6 -> v7 still requires manual review.

Third-party actions (dtolnay, dorny, Swatinem, taiki-e, docker/*, googleapis, …): auto-merge `pin` (tag -> its current SHA, no code change) and `patch` only. `digest` updates — a SHA-pinned tag re-pointed to new code — are deliberately NOT auto-merged and fall through to a manual PR. Unlike a Docker sha256, action source is human-reviewable, and these publishers do not share GitHub's trust boundary, so a digest bump is reviewed before it runs with the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN. This is the standing enforcement of debt/2026-05-30-github-actions-unpinned-sha.md.
Auto-merge patch updates for stable (v1.0.0+) cargo and npm dependencies. Pre-v1.0 (0.x.y) deps stay manual — SemVer isn't binding below 1.0 and Rust/npm 0.x patches can include behavioural changes

Pin rand_core_06 cargo alias at v0.6 — the alias name explicitly documents the deliberate version pin (v0.6 API is required by a transitive crypto consumer). Any bump silently breaks the pin intent and gets closed manually (see PR #122). Revisit if the alias is removed from Cargo.toml

customManagers.description: Rust-crate tools pinned inline via taiki-e/install-action `with: tool: <crate>@<ver>,<crate>@<ver>` syntax, plus the standalone cargo-deny pin in the audit job. install-action's manifest silently advances unpinned tools, so the project pins versions inline. Renovate's github-actions manager doesn't reach inside `with:` values, so without this manager those pins stay frozen. Tools are comma-joined in one `tool:` value, so the regex matches each `<crate>@<ver>` token by a hand-listed crate-name allowlist (cargo-nextest, cargo-llvm-cov, cargo-deny) rather than anchoring on `tool:` — the anchor only ever preceded the first token and would leave later tools frozen. The allowlist keeps matches crate-scoped; sqlx-cli uses a different idiom — see the second manager.

sqlx-cli is pinned via a job-level SQLX_CLI_VERSION env var rather than install-action's `tool:` syntax (PR #288 moved it because install-action has no sqlx-cli manifest and was falling through to a 2-minute cargo install — the env var is now the single source of truth referenced by both the actions/cache key and the cargo install fallback). The env-var form doesn't match the `tool:` regex, so it needs its own manager. depNameTemplate hard-codes the crate name because the env-var name alone isn't crate-shaped.
